candidate.content: In a pick-clean-then-place task targeting a soapbar, navigating to and opening a closed cabinet first (cabinet_1) revealed only non-target objects (soapbottle_2, spraybottle_2). Subsequently navigating to an open surface (countertop_1) revealed the target object (soapbar_1), which was successfully taken. The trajectory reached target acquisition in 4 actions across 2 inspected locations. This is feasibility evidence that inspecting a closed receptacle before an open surface can lead to successful target acquisition; it does not establish that this ordering is faster or preferable to inspecting the open surface first.
candidate.scope: ALFWorld pick-clean-then-place tasks where the target object type (e.g., soapbar) is known but not visible from the room center, and both closed storage receptacles and open surfaces are available in the admissible action list. Endpoint is target acquisition only; downstream cleaning and placement steps are not asserted.
